paper.title: On the Low-Complexity of Fair Learning for Combinatorial Multi-Armed Bandit

settings.name_in_paper: Combinatorial multi-armed bandit with fairness constraints
unmapped: Long-term fairness constraints: each arm n must receive average reward at least lambda_n (known to the learner)
Slater-type slackness: a randomized stationary policy achieves lambda_n + delta for every arm, delta > 0
Arbitrary known collection of feasible super arms (e.g. interference constraints), possibly exponentially many; at most S_max arms per super arm
Regret measured against the optimal fairness-feasible randomized stationary policy q*
Computational complexity measured in number of comparisons M per round
settings.definition_quote: We consider a combinatorial multi-armed bandit with $N$ arms, allowing for the simultaneous selection of multiple arms in each round. ... $\{X_n(t)\}_{t\geq0}$ are independently and identically distributed (i.i.d.) Bernoulli random variables with an unknown mean $\mu_n\in(0,1]$. ... ensures fairness among arms through guaranteeing each arm $n$ to receive at least the reward $\lambda_n>0$ on average

bound.expression: Min(K*T/(eta*mu_min) + 2*sqrt(6*K*m*T*log(T)) + K*(1 + 5*pi**2/12) + 2*C_1*K*T/eta + C_2*K*pi**2/6 + (1 + log(T))/C_3*K*log(m*T/K) + C_2*K + (1 + log(T))*sqrt(6*K*m*T*log(T))/(2*C_3), m*mu_max*T)
bound.expression_latex: \min \bigg\{ \frac{NT}{\eta\mu_{\min}}  +2\sqrt{6NS_{\max}T\log T} +N\left(1+\frac{5\pi^2}{12}\right) + \frac{2C_1(M) NT}{\eta} + C_2(M) \frac{N\pi^2}{6}  + \frac{1+\log T}{C_3(M)}N\log \frac{S_{\max}T}{N} + C_2(M) N + \frac{\left(1+\log T\right)\sqrt{6NS_{\max}T\log T}}{2C_3(M)}, S_{\max}\mu_{\max}T\bigg\}

symbols.alpha_M: M/|S|, probability that the random pick includes the max-weight super arm
symbols.M: number of randomly picked super arms per round

conditions: Bernoulli rewards with means in (0,1], mu_min > 0
slackness delta > 0: a randomized stationary policy achieves lambda_n + delta for all n

source.label: prop:regret
source.quote: [Cumulative Regret] Under the \lc{} algorithm with $\epsilon\leq \delta/2$, the cumulative regret $\text{Reg}(T)$ over consecutive $T$ rounds can be bounded from above as follows: ... where $C_1(M)\triangleq (\alpha^2(M)-3\alpha(M)+2)/\alpha^2(M)$, $C_2(M)\triangleq 1/\alpha(M) -1$ and $C_3(M)\triangleq -\log (1-\alpha(M))$.

results.notes: Paper's N (number of base arms) mapped to K; S_max (max arms per super arm) mapped to m. Regret is against the optimal fairness-constrained randomized stationary policy q*, defined via means (pseudo-regret); mapped comparator to best_policy. Proposition is numbered by its own counter (first proposition). Note mu_max is not defined in the paper.

symbols.M: number of randomly picked super arms per round

results.notes: Derived from Proposition 1 in a table/remark, not a formal statement. With M=|S| the table gives O_tilde(sqrt(T)) regret and zero-violation point O(T^{5/6}); with eta=0, linear regret.

source.label: prop:zero_violation
source.quote: [Zero Cumulative Fairness Violations] Under the \lc{} algorithm, if $\epsilon \leq  (\gamma\delta+\gamma-1)/2  $, there exists a zero violation point $t_0\triangleq g_0(\eta)/\epsilon=O(\eta/\epsilon)$ after which the zero cumulative fairness violation is achieved for any round $t\geq t_0$

results.notes: Bound on cumulative expected fairness violation (not regret); quantity 'other'. Paper's epsilon is the virtual-queue tightness parameter (eps_alg).

cited_results.cited_title: An efficient pessimistic-optimistic algorithm for stochastic linear bandits with general constraints
cited_results.setting_description: Stochastic (combinatorial/linear) bandits with general constraints; regret over T rounds plus zero cumulative constraint violation after some rounds
